──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Where a configuration value originated.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ConfigSource {\n    /// Built-in default value.\n    Default,\n    /// Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`).\n    GlobalFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml`).\n    WorkspaceFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Environment variable override.\n    EnvVar(String),\n    /// CLI argument override.\n    CliOverride,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigSource {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ConfigSource::Default => write!(f, \"built-in default\"),\n            ConfigSource::GlobalFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::EnvVar(name) => write!(f, \"{} env var\", name),\n            ConfigSource::CliOverride => write!(f, \"CLI argument\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map of config field paths to their source.\n///\n/// Used by `needle config --dump --show-source` to annotate each value.\npub type SourceMap = BTreeMap<String, ConfigSource>;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Workspace Overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Subset of configuration that can be overridden per-workspace via `.needle.yaml`.\n///\n/// Only these sections are The path fields (`default`, `home`) are simply ignored if set.\nconst NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS: &[&str] = &[\"worker\", \"limits\", \"health\", \"telemetry\"];\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Top-level Config\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Fully resolved NEEDLE configuration.\n///\n/// Loaded once at boot, immutable during a session.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Config {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub agent: AgentConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub worker: WorkerConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub workspace: WorkspaceConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub strands: StrandsConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub telemetry: TelemetryConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub prompt: PromptConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub health: HealthConfig,\n    /// Provider/model concurrency and rate limits.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub limits: LimitsConfig,\n    /// Per-model token pricing (USD per million tokens).\n    #[serde(default = \"crate::cost::default_pricing\")]\n    pub pricing: PricingConfig,\n    /// Daily budget thresholds for cost enforcement.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub budget: BudgetConfig,\n    /// Verification commands run after agent success, before accepting closure.\n    /// Legacy format — prefer `gates` for new configurations.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub verification: Vec<String>,\n    /// Pluggable validation gates.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub gates: Vec<GateConfig>,\n    /// Self-modification (hot-reload) configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub self_modification: SelfModificationConfig,\n    /// FABRIC live dashboard forwarding.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub fabric: FabricConfig,\n    /// Supervisor detection configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub supervisor: SupervisorConfig,\n    /// Outcome handling configuration (failure circuit-breaker).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub outcome: OutcomeConfig,\n}\n\nimpl Config {\n    /// Expand all tilde (~) paths to absolute paths using $HOME.\n    ///\n    /// This must be called after deserialization to ensure all paths\n    /// like `~/.needle` are expanded to `/home/user/.needle`.\n    /// Paths without tildes are left unchanged.\n    pub fn expand_tildes(&mut self) {\n        // workspace section\n        self.workspace.default = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.default);\n        self.workspace.home = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.home);\n\n        // agent section\n        self.agent.adapters_dir = expand_tilde(&self.agent.adapters_dir);\n\n        // strands.explore section\n        self.strands.explore.workspace_root = expand_tilde(&self.strands.explore.workspace_root);\n        self.strands.explore.workspaces = expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.explore.workspaces);\n\n        // strands.weave section\n        self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces =\n            expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces);\n\n        // strands.splice section\n        self.strands.splice.report_workspace =\n            expand_tilde_option(&self.strands.splice.report_workspace);\n\n        // strands.pulse.scanners[].command paths are strings, not PathBuf, so skip\n\n        // strands.reflect section - no PathBuf fields\n\n        // strands.learning section\n        self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file =\n            expand_tilde(&self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file);\n\n        // telemetry section\n        if let Some(ref mut log_dir) = self.telemetry.file_sink.log_dir {\n            *log_dir = expand_tilde(log_dir);\n        }\n\n        // health section\n        self.health.heartbeat_dir = expand_tilde_option(&self.health.heartbeat_dir);\n\n        // supervisor section\n        self.supervisor.heartbeat_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.heartbeat_path);\n        self.supervisor.socket_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.socket_path);\n\n        // prompt section\n        self.prompt.context_files = expand_tilde_vec(&self.prompt.context_files);\n\n        // self_modification section\n        self.self_modification.canary_workspace =\n            expand_tilde(&self.self_modification.canary_workspace);\n\n        // prompt.variants[].content_file\n        for variants in self.prompt.variants.values_mut() {\n            for variant in variants {\n                variant.content_file = expand_tilde(&variant.content_file);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Config validation\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single config validation error.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ConfigError {\n    /// Dot-separated field path (e.g., `agent.default`).\n    pub field: String,\n    /// Human-readable explanation.\n    pub message: String,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, \"{}: {}\", self.field, self.message)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// CLI overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// CLI-level overrides applied after all file-based config loading.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct CliOverrides {\n    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    pub worker_name: Option<String>,\n    pub agent_binary: Option<String>,\n    pub max_workers: Option<u32>,\n    pub explore_workspace_root: Option<PathBuf>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ConfigLoader\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Loads and validates NEEDLE configuration.\npub struct ConfigLoader;\n\nimpl ConfigLoader {\n    /// Load global config from `~/.config/needle/config.yaml`.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config (not an error).\n    pub fn load_global() -> Result<Config> {\n        let path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n        Self::load_from_path(&path)\n    }\n\n    /// Load config from a specific path.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config.\n    pub fn load_from_path(path: &Path) -> Result<Config> {\n        if !path.exists() {\n            let mut config = Config::default();\n            config.expand_tildes();\n            return Ok(config);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        let mut config: Config = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        config.expand_tildes();\n        Ok(config)\n    }\n\n    /// Load workspace overrides from `.needle.yaml` in the given workspace root.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if the file does not exist. Emits warnings for\n    /// non-overridable keys found in the workspace config.\n    pub fn load_workspace(workspace_root: &Path) -> Result<Option<WorkspaceOverrides>> {\n        let path = workspace_root.join(\".needle.yaml\");\n        if !path.exists() {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        // Check for non-overridable keys and warn.\n        Self::warn_non_overridable_keys(&text, &path)?;\n\n        let overrides: WorkspaceOverrides = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(Some(overrides))\n    }\n\n    /// Warn about non-overridable top-level keys in workspace config YAML.\n    fn warn_non_overridable_keys(yaml_text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n        let value: serde_yaml::Value = serde_yaml::from_str(yaml_text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        if let serde_yaml::Value::Mapping(map) = value {\n            for key in map.keys() {\n                if let serde_yaml::Value::String(key_str) = key {\n                    if NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS.contains(&key_str.as_str()) {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            key = %key_str,\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            \"workspace config contains non-overridable setting '{}' — ignored\",\n                            key_str,\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Apply workspace overrides to a config.\n    ///\n    /// Only overridable fields are applied. Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n8\t\n9\t1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n10\t\n11\t2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n12\t\n13\t3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n14\t\n15\t4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n16\t\n17\t5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n18\t\n19\t6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## Architecture Overview\n24\t\n25\tNEEDLE is composed of five Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n\n1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n\n2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n\n3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n\n4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n\n5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n\n6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\nNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ Plan.md already states the design intent (`docs/plan/plan.md:115`, `:1699-1718`): \"Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated.\" The implementation matches the word \"warns\" literally and does not go further.\n10\t\n11\t**What exists:** `RateLimiter::check_system_resources` (`src/rate_limit/mod.rs:350-400`) reads `/proc/loadavg` and `/proc/meminfo` and emits an `EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated` telemetry event plus a `tracing::warn!` when thresholds are crossed. Its return value is not consulted by any caller to gate or delay anything — it is a pure side-effecting observability call.\n12\t\n13\t**Where it's called:** only from `do_dispatch()` (`src/worker/mod.rs:1607-1612`) — inside an **already-running** worker's loop, immediately before executing a bead that worker has **already claimed**. It is never called during `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs:861-868`, a plain sequential `init_step(...)` call with no CPU/RAM gate before or during it), and never called during the `--count=N` sequential-launch sequence.\n14\t\n15\t**Launch spacing is a fixed interval, not load-adaptive:** `src/cli/mod.rs:637-638` — `if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 { std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs)); }`, where `stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds` defaults to `2` (`docs/plan/plan.md:1739`). This delay is the same whether the box is idle or already at 3x its core count in load average.\n16\t\n17\t**The gap this leaves, previously diagnosed operationally (2026-07-19, lab):** `worker_construction` is a genuinely slow (~5s) init step — it builds the agent adapter and warms the provider proxy connection. Under CPU saturation it can overrun whatever margin it has and the OS terminates the process before it completes — no Rust panic, no backtrace, just a worker that silently vanishes seconds after being launched. This was diagnosed by direct comparison: an identical launch command died twice at load ~2.5, then succeeded 90 minutes later at load ~0.74 with `worker_construction completed in 4992ms` — just under whatever margin exists. (The precise OS-level kill mechanism — cgroup pressure, systemd deadline, scheduler starvation past some other bound — was not re-diagnosed as part of this codebase review; what *is* newly confirmed by this review is that NEEDLE's own code has no gate that would prevent launching into this condition in the first place.) NEEDLE's own 60-second boot timeout (`src/cli/mod.rs:870-875`) cannot catch this class of failure, since it only evaluates *after* `init_step` returns — a process killed mid-step by something outside NEEDLE never reaches that check.\n18\t\n19\tNet effect: the one place in the codebase that actually reads system load (`check_system_resources`) is checked at the wrong point in the lifecycle to prevent the failure mode plan.md already anticipated in prose. It protects an already-running worker from starting *another* bead under saturation; it does nothing to stop a *new* worker from being launched into saturation in the first place, or to slow down a batch launch that is itself the cause of the saturation.\n20\t\n21\t## Decision\n22\t\n23\t1. **12.1 — Gate `worker_construction` on system resources, not just `do_dispatch`.** Before entering `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs`, around line 861), call `check_system_resources()` (or a renamed/generalized variant, since it's no longer rate-limit-specific once used here). If saturated (same thresholds already defined for `FleetCpuSaturated`), do not proceed into the slow construction step — retry with backoff (a few seconds, capped) until load drops below threshold or a max-wait is hit, at which point fail the launch with a clear, actionable error (`\"deferred N times, system still saturated (load X vs threshold Y) — launch aborted, retry when load drops\"`) rather than letting the OS silently kill an in-flight construction. This turns an unexplained vanished-worker into an explicit, loggable, retryable outcome.\n24\t2. **12.2 — Load-adaptive launch staggering.** Replace the fixed `launch_stagger_seconds` sleep in the `--count=N` sequential-launch path with a check against current load before each subsequent launch: if load is below a comfortable threshold, use the existing (short) default delay; if above it, extend the wait (bounded, with a cap) until load recedes or the cap is hit. This directly targets the failure mode where the *stagger itself* is what's supposed to prevent thundering-herd saturation but currently does so blindly regardless of whether the previous launches already pushed load past a safe point.\n25\t3. **12.3 — Apply the same gate to `needle supervise`'s auto-scale spawn path**, not only the CLI's `--count=N` path — the supervisor daemon (`src/supervisor/mod.rs`) is the other place new workers get launched, and it should not spawn a worker into saturation any more than a manual `--count=N` invocation should.\n26\t4. **Ship through the existing release path**: version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`).\n27\t\n28\t## Consequences\n29\t\n30\t- Positive: closes the gap between plan.md's stated design intent (\"NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated\") and its actual behavior (monitors and warns only for an already-running worker's next-bead decision) — the fix is a matter of calling an existing function from two more call sites and consulting its result, not building new infrastructure.\n31\t- A deferred/retried launch under 12.1 changes `needle run`'s observable behavior under load — a launch that previously either silently died or (rarely) squeaked through now explicitly waits or explicitly fails with a reason. Plan.md already states the design intent (`docs/plan/plan.md:115`, `:1699-1718`): \"Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated.\" The implementation matches the word \"warns\" literally and does not go further.\n\n**What exists:** `RateLimiter::check_system_resources` (`src/rate_limit/mod.rs:350-400`) reads `/proc/loadavg` and `/proc/meminfo` and emits an `EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated` telemetry event plus a `tracing::warn!` when thresholds are crossed. Its return value is not consulted by any caller to gate or delay anything — it is a pure side-effecting observability call.\n\n**Where it's called:** only from `do_dispatch()` (`src/worker/mod.rs:1607-1612`) — inside an **already-running** worker's loop, immediately before executing a bead that worker has **already claimed**. It is never called during `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs:861-868`, a plain sequential `init_step(...)` call with no CPU/RAM gate before or during it), and never called during the `--count=N` sequential-launch sequence.\n\n**Launch spacing is a fixed interval, not load-adaptive:** `src/cli/mod.rs:637-638` — `if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 { std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs)); }`, where `stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds` defaults to `2` (`docs/plan/plan.md:1739`). This delay is the same whether the box is idle or already at 3x its core count in load average.\n\n**The gap this leaves, previously diagnosed operationally (2026-07-19, lab):** `worker_construction` is a genuinely slow (~5s) init step — it builds the agent adapter and warms the provider proxy connection. Under CPU saturation it can overrun whatever margin it has and the OS terminates the process before it completes — no Rust panic, no backtrace, just a worker that silently vanishes seconds after being launched. This was diagnosed by direct comparison: an identical launch command died twice at load ~2.5, then succeeded 90 minutes later at load ~0.74 with `worker_construction completed in 4992ms` — just under whatever margin exists. (The precise OS-level kill mechanism — cgroup pressure, systemd deadline, scheduler starvation past some other bound — was not re-diagnosed as part of this codebase review; what *is* newly confirmed by this review is that NEEDLE's own code has no gate that would prevent launching into this condition in the first place.) NEEDLE's own 60-second boot timeout (`src/cli/mod.rs:870-875`) cannot catch this class of failure, since it only evaluates *after* `init_step` returns — a process killed mid-step by something outside NEEDLE never reaches that check.\n\nNet effect: the one place in the codebase that actually reads system load (`check_system_resources`) is checked at the wrong point in the lifecycle to prevent the failure mode plan.md already anticipated in prose. It protects an already-running worker from starting *another* bead under saturation; it does nothing to stop a *new* worker from being launched into saturation in the first place, or to slow down a batch launch that is itself the cause of the saturation.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **12.1 — Gate `worker_construction` on system resources, not just `do_dispatch`.** Before entering `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs`, around line 861), call `check_system_resources()` (or a renamed/generalized variant, since it's no longer rate-limit-specific once used here). If saturated (same thresholds already defined for `FleetCpuSaturated`), do not proceed into the slow construction step — retry with backoff (a few seconds, capped) until load drops below threshold or a max-wait is hit, at which point fail the launch with a clear, actionable error (`\"deferred N times, system still saturated (load X vs threshold Y) — launch aborted, retry when load drops\"`) rather than letting the OS silently kill an in-flight construction. This turns an unexplained vanished-worker into an explicit, loggable, retryable outcome.\n2. **12.2 — Load-adaptive launch staggering.** Replace the fixed `launch_stagger_seconds` sleep in the `--count=N` sequential-launch path with a check against current load before each subsequent launch: if load is below a comfortable threshold, use the existing (short) default delay; if above it, extend the wait (bounded, with a cap) until load recedes or the cap is hit. This directly targets the failure mode where the *stagger itself* is what's supposed to prevent thundering-herd saturation but currently does so blindly regardless of whether the previous launches already pushed load past a safe point.\n3. **12.3 — Apply the same gate to `needle supervise`'s auto-scale spawn path**, not only the CLI's `--count=N` path — the supervisor daemon (`src/supervisor/mod.rs`) is the other place new workers get launched, and it should not spawn a worker into saturation any more than a manual `--count=N` invocation should.\n4. **Ship through the existing release path**: version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`).\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Positive: closes the gap between plan.md's stated design intent (\"NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated\") and its actual behavior (monitors and warns only for an already-running worker's next-bead decision) — the fix is a matter of calling an existing function from two more call sites and consulting its result, not building new infrastructure.\n- A deferred/retried launch under 12.1 changes `needle run`'s observable behavior under load — a launch that previously either silently died or (rarely) squeaked through now explicitly waits or explicitly fails with a reason. Any external tooling (scripts, the fleet launcher wrapper) that assumes `needle run` returns immediately after backgrounding into tmux needs to tolerate a longer, bounded wait under saturation.\n- 12.2's adaptive stagger means a large `--count=N` batch launch on an already-busy host will take longer wall-clock time than before — this is the intended tradeoff (slower but reliable launches vs. fast but silently-lossy ones), consistent with the existing operational practice of manually staggering launches while watching `uptime`.\n- Does not address the separate, harder question of *how many workers is too many* for a given host long-term (that's the \"ready-bead supply is the real ceiling, not hardware\" finding from a separate operational audit) — this ADR is scoped to preventing a single launch from being silently killed mid-construction, not to fleet-sizing policy in general.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `docs/plan/plan.md:115`, `:1699-1718` (stated design intent: \"NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated\").\n- `src/rate_limit/mod.rs:350-400` (`check_system_resources`, reads `/proc/loadavg`/`/proc/meminfo`, emits `FleetCpuSaturated`, return value unused by callers).\n- `src/worker/mod.rs:1607-1612` (only call site: `do_dispatch()`, already-running worker, already-claimed bead).\n- `src/cli/mod.rs:861-868` (`worker_construction` init step, no resource gate before/during); ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Entry point called from `main`.\npub fn run() -> Result<()> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    match cli.command {\n        CliCommand::Run {\n            workspace,\n            agent,\n            count,\n            identifier,\n            timeout,\n            resume,\n            hot_reload,\n        } => cmd_run(\n            workspace, agent, count, identifier, timeout, resume, hot_reload,\n        ),\n        CliCommand::Stop { all, identifier } => cmd_stop(all, identifier),\n        CliCommand::Cleanup { all, identifier } => cmd_cleanup(all, identifier),\n        CliCommand::List { format } => cmd_list(format),\n        CliCommand::Attach { identifier } => cmd_attach(&identifier),\n        CliCommand::Status {\n            format,\n            by_worker,\n            cost,\n            since,\n            until,\n            idle_strands,\n        } =>     } => cmd_logs(follow, filter, since, until, format),\n        CliCommand::ConfigCmd {\n            get,\n            set,\n            dump,\n            show_source,\n        } => cmd_config(get, cmd_version();\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        CliCommand::TestAgent { name } => cmd_test_agent(&name),\n        CliCommand::Canary { status } => cmd_canary(status),\n        CliCommand::Upgrade { check } => cmd_upgrade(check),\n        CliCommand::Rollback => cmd_rollback(),\n        CliCommand::Reflect { workspace, force } => cmd_reflect(workspace, force),\n        CliCommand::UpdateRules { output } => cmd_update_rules(output),\n        CliCommand::Stats {\n            by,\n            since,\n            until,\n            format,\n        } => cmd_stats(by, Command handlers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `needle run` — launch a worker.\n///\n/// Always creates dedicated tmux sessions for workers, even when invoked from\n/// inside an existing tmux session. The only exception is a re-entrant inner\n/// invocation launched by `launch_in_tmux()`, which is identified by the\n/// `NEEDLE_INNER=1` environment variable and runs the worker directly.\nfn cmd_run(\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    count: u32,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    resume: bool,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Determine workspace root (CLI arg → canonicalized, else global default).\n    let workspace_root = if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n    } else {\n        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n        global.workspace.default.clone()\n    };\n\n    // Load full resolved config (global → workspace .needle.yaml → env → CLI).\n    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n        agent_binary: agent.clone(),\n        max_workers: None,\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let (mut config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n\n    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n        config.agent.timeout = t;\n    }\n\n    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n        config.self_modification.hot_reload = hr;\n    }\n\n    if resume {\n        // Hot-reload resume: inherit worker identity from --identifier,\n        // load state from heartbeat file + registry, continue from SELECTING.\n        let worker_id = identifier\n            .clone()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n\n        // Load resume state from heartbeat and registry.\n        let resume_state = crate::upgrade::ResumeState::load(&config, &worker_id)?;\n\n        // Emit upgrade.completed telemetry.\n        let current_hash = crate::upgrade::file_hash(\n            &std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?,\n        )\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"unknown\".to_string());\n\n        match &resume_state {\n            Some(state) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    worker = %worker_id,\n                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n                    beads_processed = state.beads_processed,\n                    session = %state.session,\n                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload\"\n                );\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    worker = %worker_id,\n                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload (no prior state found)\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        let tel = crate::telemetry::Telemetry::from_config(worker_id.clone(), &config.telemetry)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"hook telemetry init failed, falling back\");\n                crate::telemetry::Telemetry::new(worker_id.clone())\n            });\n        tel.emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::UpgradeCompleted {\n            new_hash: current_hash,\n        })?;\n\n        return run_worker(config, worker_id);\n    }\n\n    if is_needle_inner() {\n        // Re-entrant inner invocation launched by launch_in_tmux() — run\n        // the worker directly inside the dedicated session already created.\n        let worker_id = identifier\n            .clone()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n        let agent_name = agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(&config.agent.default);\n        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n        tracing::info!(worker = %worker_id, session = %session_name, \"starting worker (inner re-entrant invocation)\");\n        run_worker(config, worker_id)\n    } else {\n        // Always create dedicated tmux sessions, even if already inside tmux.\n        launch_workers(\n            config, workspace, agent, count, identifier, timeout, hot_reload,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// Launch `count` workers in separate tmux sessions with staggered startup delays.\npub fn launch_workers(\n    config: Config,\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    count: u32,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let agent_name = agent\n        .as_deref()\n        .unwrap_or(&config.agent.default)\n        .to_string();\n    let stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds;\n    let max_workers = config.worker.max_workers;\n\n    if count == 0 {\n        bail!(\"--count must be at least 1\");\n    }\n    if count as usize > NATO_ALPHABET.len() {\n        bail!(\n            \"--count {} exceeds the maximum of {} (NATO alphabet size)\",\n            count,\n            NATO_ALPHABET.len()\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Enforce max_workers cap (0 means unlimited).\n    let effective_count = if max_workers > 0 && count > max_workers {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            requested = count,\n            capped_to = max_workers,\n            \"count exceeds max_workers; capping\"\n        );\n        eprintln!(\n            \"Warning: --count {count} exceeds max_workers={max_workers}; launching {max_workers} workers\"\n        );\n        max_workers\n    } else {\n        count\n    };\n\n    // --identifier is only meaningful for a single worker.\n    if effective_count > 1 && identifier.is_some() {\n        bail!(\"--identifier cannot be combined with --count > 1; identifiers are auto-assigned from the NATO alphabet\");\n    }\n\n    // Detect existing sessions to avoid name collisions.\n    let occupied = occupied_worker_ids(&agent_name)?;\n    if !occupied.is_empty() {\n        tracing::info!(\n            occupied = ?occupied,\n            \"found existing worker sessions\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Reject --identifier collision early.\n    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n        if occupied.contains(id) {\n            bail!(\n                \"worker '{}' is already running in session 'needle-{}-{}'\",\n                id,\n                agent_name,\n                id\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Build the list of worker IDs, skipping occupied names.\n    let worker_ids: Vec<String> = if effective_count == 1 {\n        vec![identifier.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {\n            // Pick the first available NATO name.\n            NATO_ALPHABET\n                .iter()\n                .find(|name| !occupied.contains(**name))\n                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string())\n        })]\n    } else {\n        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(effective_count as usize);\n        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n            if ids.len() >= effective_count as usize {\n                break;\n            }\n            if occupied.contains(*name) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    worker_id = %name,\n                    \"skipping occupied worker name\"\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n            ids.push(name.to_string());\n        }\n        if ids.len() < effective_count as usize {\n            bail!(\n                \"cannot launch {} workers — only {} NATO names available ({} occupied)\",\n                effective_count,\n                ids.len(),\n                occupied.len()\n            );\n        }\n        ids\n    };\n\n    for (seq, worker_id) in worker_ids.iter().enumerate() {\n        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_id = %worker_id,\n            sequence = seq,\n            total = effective_count,\n            session = %session_name,\n            \"launching worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Stagger: sleep before launching subsequent workers.\n        if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 {\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs));\n        }\n\n        launch_in_tmux(\n            &session_name,\n            workspace.clone(),\n            agent.clone(),\n            Some(worker_id.clone()),\n            timeout,\n            hot_reload,\n        )?;\n\n        println!(\n            \"[{}/{}] Started worker '{}' in tmux session: {session_name}\",\n            seq + 1,\n            effective_count,\n            worker_id\n        );\n    }\n\n    let sanitized_agent = sanitize_session_name(&agent_name);\n    if effective_count > 1 {\n        println!(\n            \"\\nStarted {effective_count} workers (stagger: {stagger_secs}s between launches).\"\n        );\n        println!(\"Attach to a worker with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-<name>\");\n    } else {\n        let worker_id = &worker_ids[0];\n        println!(\"Attach with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-{worker_id}\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Initialize the tracing subscriber with OTLP layer if configured.\n///\n/// This must be called before any tracing spans are created so that the OTLP\n/// layer can export them to the configured collector.\n///\n/// Note: Shutdown is handled by the OtlpSink in the telemetry module, not here.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n    worker_id: String,\n    session_id: String,\n    config: &crate::config::Config,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TracerProvider;\n    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n\n    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n\n    // Check if OTLP is enabled\n    if !config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled {\n        // No OTLP - just initialize with fmt layer\n        let fmt_layer = tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n            .with_ansi(use_ansi);\n        tracing_subscriber::registry()\n            .with(fmt_layer)\n            .try_init()\n            .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // OTLP is enabled - create the OTLP layer inline\n    // We create it inline to avoid type erasure issues with boxed layers\n    let otlp_config = &config.telemetry.otlp_sink;\n\n    // Build resource attributes\n    let resource = crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_resource(\n        &worker_id,\n        &session_id,\n        otlp_config,\n        Some(&config.agent.default),\n        None, // model - not available in AgentConfig\n        config.workspace.default.to_str(),\n    )\n    .context(\"failed to build OTel resource\")?;\n\n    // Create drop channel for tracing layer\n    let (drop_tx, mut drop_rx) =\n        tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<crate::telemetry::otlp::DropEvent>();\n    tokio::spawn(async move {\n        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                signal = drop.signal.as_str(),\n                dropped_count = drop.dropped_count,\n                \"OTLP tracing layer export failure\"\n            );\n        }\n    });\n\n    // Build exporters and tracer provider based on protocol\n    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match otlp_config.protocol.as_str() {\n        \"grpc\" => {\n            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n        }\n        \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => {\n            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_http_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n        }\n        other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n    };\n\n    // Create the OpenTelemetry tracing layer\n    let otlp_layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer(\"needle\"));\n\n    // Create a fmt layer that works with any subscriber implementing LookupSpan\n    // We build this after the OTLP layer to ensure proper type compatibility\n    let subscriber = tracing_subscriber::registry().with(otlp_layer).with(\n        tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n            .with_ansi(use_ansi),\n    );\n\n    subscriber\n        .try_init()\n        .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber with OTLP\")?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// No-op tracing initialization when OTLP feature is disabled.\n#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\nfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n    _worker_id: String,\n    _session_id: String,\n    _config: &crate::config::Config,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n\n    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n\n    // Initialize with just the platforms).\n#[cfg(not(target_os = \"android\"))]\nfn use_ansi() -> bool {\n    atty::is(atty::Stream::Stderr)\n}\n\n/// Helper function for Android (no ANSI).\n#[cfg(target_os = \"android\")]\nfn use_ansi() -> bool {\n    false\n}\n\n/// Generate a session ID for a worker.\n///\n/// Uses the telemetry module's session ID generator.\nfn generate_session_id_for_worker() -> String {\n    crate::telemetry::generate_session_id()\n}\n\n/// Start the worker state machine (called when inside tmux or for direct mode).\n///\n/// Creates telemetry and the tokio runtime *before* any other initialization\n/// so that `worker.booting` is the very first JSONL event. Each subsequent\n/// init step is wrapped with `init.step.started` / `init.step.completed` so a\n/// silent hang pinpoints the exact blocking call.\nfn run_worker(config: Config, worker_name: String) -> Result<()> {\n    let boot_start = Instant::now();\n    let qualified_id = format!(\"{}-{}\", config.agent.default, worker_name);\n\n    // Phase 0: create tokio runtime + telemetry, emit worker.booting immediately.\n    // Emit eprintln diagnostics before each step so hangs are visible even if telemetry fails.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: creating tokio runtime...\");\n    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().context(\"failed to create tokio runtime\")?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created\");\n\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: initializing tracing subscriber...\");\n    let session_id = generate_session_id_for_worker();\n    init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: tracing subscriber initialized\");\n\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: creating telemetry...\");\n    let telemetry =\n        Telemetry::from_config(qualified_id.clone(), &config.telemetry).unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create hook-enabled telemetry, falling back\");\n            Telemetry::new(qualified_id.clone())\n        });\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: telemetry created\");\n\n    // Emit worker.booting SYNCHRONOUSLY before starting the async writer.\n    // This guarantees the event is written to disk even if start_and_wait() hangs.\n    // Fixes the silent pre-init deadlock where the JSONL file is created but empty.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: emitting worker.booting event (sync)...\");\n    telemetry.emit_sync(EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n        worker_name: worker_name.clone(),\n        version: env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string(),\n    })?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: worker.booting written to disk\");\n\n    // Start the async writer thread after worker.booting is on disk.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: starting telemetry writer thread...\");\n    rt.block_on(telemetry.start_and_wait())\n        .context(\"writer thread failed to start\")?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: writer thread started\");\n\n    // Phase 1: bead store discovery.\n    // Use BfCliBeadStore for atomic server-selected bead claiming.\n    let store: Arc<dyn crate::bead_store::BeadStore> =\n        Arc::new(init_step(\"bead_store_discover\", &telemetry, || {\n            let bf_store = crate::bead_store::BfCliBeadStore::discover(\n                config.workspace.default.clone(),\n                None,                       // model: do not filter by model — beads are untagged\n                Some(\"needle\".to_string()), // harness\n                Some(env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string()), // harness_version\n            )\n            .context(\"failed to locate bf CLI for bead store\")?;\n\n            // Run bead-forge version handshake to detect known-bad versions.\n            let bf_path = &bf_store.bf_path;\n            let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()\n                .context(\"failed to create runtime for version check\")?;\n            rt.block_on(crate::bead_store::run_version_handshake(bf_path));\n\n            Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(bf_store)\n        })?);\n\n    // Phase 2: resource check before worker construction.\n    // Check system resources (CPU and memory) before entering the slow\n    // (~5s) worker_construction step. If saturated, retry with bounded\n    // backoff rather than proceeding into a step that may be killed by\n    // the OS due to resource pressure.\n    const MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 120; // Maximum total wait time\n    const RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS: u64 = 5; // Initial retry delay\n    let mut resource_wait_total = 0u64;\n    let mut resource_retry_delay = RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS;\n\n    loop {\n        match crate::rate_limit::RateLimiter::check_system_resources_for_launch(\n            config.worker.cpu_load_warn,\n            config.worker.memory_free_warn_mb,\n            &telemetry,\n        ) {\n            Ok(()) => {\n                // Resources are acceptable, proceed to worker_construction\n                break;\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                if resource_wait_total >= MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS {\n                    // Still saturated after max wait, fail the launch explicitly\n                    telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                        deferred_count: resource_wait_total / resource_retry_delay,\n                        total_wait_secs: resource_wait_total,\n                        reason: format!(\n                            \"system still saturated after {}s wait: {}\",\n                            MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS, e\n                        ),\n                    })?;\n                    bail!(\n                        \"worker launch deferred {} times ({}s total wait), system still saturated: {}. Launch aborted — retry when load drops\",\n                        resource_wait_total / resource_retry_delay,\n                        resource_wait_total,\n                        e\n                    );\n                }\n\n                // Resources are saturated, wait and retry\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    wait_secs = resource_retry_delay,\n                    total_waited_secs = resource_wait_total,\n                    \"system resources saturated, deferring worker construction\"\n                );\n\n                telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                    deferred_count: resource_wait_total / resource_retry_delay + 1,\n                    total_wait_secs: resource_wait_total + resource_retry_delay,\n                    reason: format!(\"system saturated: {}\", e),\n                })?;\n\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(resource_retry_delay));\n                resource_wait_total += resource_retry_delay;\n\n                // Exponential backoff with cap at 30 seconds\n                resource_retry_delay = std::cmp::min(resource_retry_delay * 2, 30);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Phase 3: worker construction (heavy — prompt loading, adapter discovery, etc.).\n    let mut worker = init_step(\"worker_construction\", &telemetry, || {\n        Ok(Worker::new_with_telemetry(\n            config,\n            worker_name.clone(),\n            store,\n            telemetry.clone(),\n        ))\n    })?;\n\n    // Boot timeout guard: self-abort if init took >60 s.\n    let elapsed_ms = boot_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n    if elapsed_ms > 60_000 {\n        telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms })?;\n        bail!(\"boot exceeded 60 s ({elapsed_ms} ms), aborting\");\n    }\n\n    eprintln!(\n        \"NEEDLE worker boot: all init steps completed in {elapsed_ms}ms, starting worker loop...\"\n    );\n    let result = rt.block_on(worker.run())?;\n\n    tracing::info!(final_state = %result, \"worker finished\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Emit start/complete telemetry around a fallible initialization step.\n///\n/// Each step's completion is force-flushed to disk so that if a subsequent\n/// step blocks indefinitely, the telemetry log shows exactly where it stopped.\n/// Also emits eprintln diagnostics for visibility even if telemetry hangs.\nfn init_step<T, F>(name: &str, tel: &Telemetry, f: F) -> Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: FnOnce() -> Result<T>,\n{\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: starting init step '{name}'...\");\n    tel.emit(EventKind::InitStepStarted {\n        step: name.to_string(),\n    })?;\n    let t = Instant::now();\n    let result = f();\n    let elapsed = t.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n    tel.emit(EventKind::InitStepCompleted {\n        step: name.to_string(),\n        duration_ms: elapsed,\n    })?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: init step '{name}' completed in {elapsed}ms\");\n    // Force-flush so the step completion is visible before the next (potentially blocking) step.\n    tel.force_flush(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1))?;\n    result\n}\n\n/// Returns true when this process is a re-entrant inner invocation launched\n/// by `launch_in_tmux()`, indicated by `NEEDLE_INNER=1` in the environment.\nfn is_needle_inner() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"NEEDLE_INNER\").is_ok_and(|v| v == \"1\")\n}\n\n/// Create a single tmux session and re-exec self inside it with `--count 1`.\nfn launch_in_tmux(\n    session_name: &str,\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Build the command that tmux will run inside the session.\n    let self_exe = std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?;\n    let mut inner_args = vec![\"run\".to_string()];\n\n    if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n        inner_args.push(\"--workspace\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(ws.display().to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(ref a) = agent {\n        inner_args.push(\"--agent\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(a.clone());\n    }\n    // Each session runs exactly one worker; identifier is always resolved before call.\n    inner_args.push(\"--count\".to_string());\n    inner_args.push(\"1\".to_string());\n    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n        inner_args.push(\"--identifier\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(id.clone());\n    }\n    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n        inner_args.push(\"--timeout\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(t.to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n        inner_args.push(\"--hot-reload\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(hr.to_string());\n    }\n\n    // Build stderr log path: ~/.needle/logs/<session_name>.stderr.log\n    let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n    let stderr_log = format!(\"{home}/.needle/logs/{session_name}.stderr.log\");\n\n    let inner_cmd = format!(\n        \"NEEDLE_INNER=1 {} {} 2>> {}\",\n        shell_escape(&self_exe.display().to_string()),\n        inner_args\n            .iter()\n            .map(|a| shell_escape(a))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\" \"),\n        shell_escape(&stderr_log)\n    );\n\n    let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n        .args([\"new-session\", \"-d\", \"-s\", session_name, &inner_cmd])\n        .status()\n        .context(\"failed to launch tmux — is tmux installed?\")?;\n\n    if !status.success() {\n        bail!(\n            \"tmux new-session exited with status {} for session '{}'\",\n            status,\n            session_name\n        );\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Kill the entire process tree rooted at the given PID.\n///\n/// This function recursively finds all child processes and sends SIGTERM,\n/// waits for processes to exit, and sends SIGKILL to any remaining processes.\n/// Returns true if all processes were successfully terminated.\n///\n/// This is necessary because agents are spawned with setpgid(0,0), creating\n/// new process groups that are not reachable via killpg() on the parent PGID.\nfn kill_process_tree(pid: u32) -> Result<bool> {\n    use std::thread;\n\n    tracing::info!(pid, \"finding all descendant processes to terminate\");\n\n    // Collect all descendant PIDs by reading /proc\n    let descendants = find_all_descendants(pid);\n    let descendant_count = descendants.len();\n\n    if descendant_count > 0 {\n        tracing::info!(\n            pid,\n            count = descendant_count,\n            ?descendants,\n            \"found descendant processes\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Send SIGTERM to all descendants (including the original PID)\n    let all_pids: Vec<u32> = std::iter::once(pid).chain(descendants).collect();\n    tracing::info!(\n        pid,\n        count = all_pids.len(),\n        \"sending SIGTERM to process tree\"\n    );\n\n    for target_pid in &all_pids {\n        unsafe {\n            if libc::kill(*target_pid as libc::pid_t, libc::SIGTERM) == -1 {\n                let err = std::io::Error::last_os_error();\n                if err.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound {\n                    tracing::warn!(pid = target_pid, error = %err, \"SIGTERM failed\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Wait up to 5 seconds for processes to exit gracefully\n    for i in 0..50 {\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n\n        // Check if all processes are gone\n        let all_dead = all_pids\n            .iter()\n            .all(|&p| unsafe { libc::kill(p as libc::pid_t, 0) != 0 });\n\n        if all_dead {\n            tracing::info!(\n                pid,\n                \"process tree terminated gracefully after {}ms\",\n                (i + 1) * 100\n            );\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Some processes survived SIGTERM, use SIGKILL\n    tracing::warn!(pid, \"process tree survived SIGTERM, sending SIGKILL\");\n    for target_pid in &all_pids {\n        unsafe {\n            if libc::kill(*target_pid as libc::pid_t, libc::SIGKILL) == -1 {\n                let err = std::io::Error::last_os_error();\n                if err.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound {\n                    tracing::error!(pid = target_pid, error = %err, \"SIGKILL failed\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Wait up to 3 seconds for SIGKILL to take effect\n    for i in 0..30 {\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n\n        let all_dead = all_pids\n            .iter()\n            .all(|&p| unsafe { libc::kill(p as libc::pid_t, 0) != 0 });\n\n        if all_dead {\n            tracing::info!(\n                pid,\n                \"process tree terminated by SIGKILL after {}ms\",\n                (i + 1) * 100\n            );\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Check which processes are still alive\n    let still_alive: Vec<u32> = all_pids\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|&&p| unsafe { libc::kill(p as libc::pid_t, 0) == 0 })\n        .copied()\n        .collect();\n\n    if !still_alive.is_empty() {\n        tracing::error!(\n            pid,\n            ?still_alive,\n            \"process tree survived SIGKILL - {} processes still running\",\n            still_alive.len()\n        );\n    }\n\n    Ok(still_alive.is_empty())\n}\n\n/// Recursively find all descendant processes of the given PID.\n///\n/// Reads /proc to build a process tree and returns all descendant PIDs.\n/// This handles the case where agents create new process groups with setpgid(0,0).\nfn find_all_descendants(root_pid: u32) -> Vec<u32> {\n    use std::fs;\n\n    let proc_dir = Path::new(\"/proc\");\n    let mut ppid_to_children: HashMap<u32, Vec<u32>> = HashMap::new();\n\n    // First pass: build parent->children mapping\n    if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(proc_dir) {\n        for entry in entries.flatten() {\n            let pid_str = entry.file_name();\n            let pid: u32 = match pid_str.to_string_lossy().parse() {\n                Ok(p) => p,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Skip the root PID itself\n            if pid == root_pid {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Read /proc/[pid]/status to get PPID\n            let status_path = entry.path().join(\"status\");\n            if let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&status_path) {\n                let ppid = content\n                    .lines()\n                    .find(|line| line.starts_with(\"PPID:\\t\"))\n                    .and_then(|line| line.split(':').nth(1))\n                    .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse().ok());\n\n                if let Some(parent_pid) = ppid {\n                    ppid_to_children.entry(parent_pid).or_default().push(pid);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Recursive DFS to find all descendants\n    let mut descendants = Vec::new();\n    let mut visited = HashSet::new();\n    // Mark the root PID as visited to prevent cycles\n    visited.insert(root_pid);\n    find_descendants_recursive(root_pid, &ppid_to_children, &mut descendants, &mut visited);\n\n    descendants\n}\n\n/// Recursive helper to traverse process tree and collect descendants.\nfn find_descendants_recursive(\n    pid: u32,\n    ppid_to_children: &HashMap<u32, Vec<u32>>,\n    descendants: &mut Vec<u32>,\n    visited: &mut HashSet<u32>,\n) {\n    if let Some(children) = ppid_to_children.get(&pid) {\n        for &child_pid in children {\n            if visited.insert(child_pid) {\n                descendants.push(child_pid);\n                find_descendants_recursive(child_pid, ppid_to_children, descendants, visited);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a PID is a needle run process by reading /proc/[pid]/cmdline.\n///\n/// Returns true if the process command line contains \"needle run\".\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn is_needle_run_process(pid: u32) -> bool {\n    use std::fs;\n\n    let cmdline_path = Path::new(\"/proc\").join(pid.to_string()).join(\"cmdline\");\n    let cmdline_bytes = match fs::read(&cmdline_path) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(_) => return false, // Process may have exited or /proc not available\n    };\n\n    // cmdline is null-separated; convert to space-separated for checking.\n    let cmdline: String = cmdline_bytes\n        .split(|&b| b == 0)\n        .map(|args| String::from_utf8_lossy(args))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\" \");\n\n    cmdline.contains(\"needle run\")\n}\n\n/// Find the actual needle run process in a process tree.\n///\n/// Given a root PID (typically from tmux pane_pid), this function searches for\n/// needle run processes in the descendant tree. This handles the case where\n/// tmux pane_pid returns a shell PID instead of the actual needle binary.\n///\n/// Returns the PID of the needle run process if found, None otherwise.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn find_needle_process_in_tree(root_pid: u32) -> Option<u32> {\n    // First check if the root itself is a needle run process\n    if is_needle_run_process(root_pid) {\n        return Some(root_pid);\n    }\n\n    // Search descendants for needle run processes\n    let descendants = find_all_descendants(root_pid);\n    descendants\n        .into_iter()\n        .find(|&pid| is_needle_run_process(pid))\n}\n\n/// Check if any needle processes are still running after a kill attempt.\n///\n/// This function scans the process table to find all needle run processes\n/// and their descendants. This is used after a kill attempt to verify that\n/// ALL processes (needle run + dispatched agent + any descendants) are\n/// actually gone, not just the original PID we tried to kill.\n///\n/// Returns a vector of PIDs that are still running, along with their command lines.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn verify_no_needle_processes_remaining() -> Vec<(u32, String)> {\n    use std::fs;\n\n    let proc_dir = Path::new(\"/proc\");\n    let mut remaining = Vec::new();\n\n    if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(proc_dir) {\n        for entry in entries.flatten() {\n            let pid_str = entry.file_name();\n            let pid: u32 = match pid_str.to_string_lossy().parse() {\n                Ok(p) => p,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Read /proc/[pid]/cmdline to check if this is a needle process\n            let cmdline_path = entry.path().join(\"cmdline\");\n            let cmdline_bytes = match fs::read(&cmdline_path) {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(_) => continue, // Process may have exited\n            };\n\n            // cmdline is null-separated; convert to space-separated for checking.\n            let cmdline: String = cmdline_bytes\n                .split(|&b| b == 0)\n                .map(|args| String::from_utf8_lossy(args))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\" \");\n\n            // Check if this is a needle run process or a related subprocess\n            if cmdline.contains(\"needle run\") || cmdline.contains(\"NEEDLE_INNER\") {\n                remaining.push((pid, cmdline));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    remaining\n}\n\n/// `needle stop` — kill the full process tree for worker processes.\n///\n/// This command kills the parent needle run process, its bash -c prompt wrapper,\n/// and the dispatched claude subprocess (full tree, not just the tmux session).\n/// It verifies the PID is actually gone before printing success.\nfn cmd_stop(all: bool, identifier: Option<String>) -> Result<()> {\n    if !all && identifier.is_none() {\n        bail!(\"specify --all or --identifier <NAME>\");\n    }\n\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No needle sessions running.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // Find target sessions by name\n    let targets: Vec<TmuxSession> = if all {\n        sessions.clone()\n    } else {\n        let id = identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"\");\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.name.contains(id))\n            .cloned()\n            .collect()\n    };\n\n    if targets.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No matching sessions found.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    for session in &targets {\n        tracing::info!(session = %session.name, \"stopping worker\");\n\n        // Get the PID from the tmux session\n        let tmux_pid = match session.pid {\n            Some(p) => p,\n            None => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Warning: no PID found for session '{}', skipping process tree kill\",\n                    session.name\n                );\n                // Still kill the session for cleanup\n                let _ = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n                    .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", &session.name])\n                    .status();\n                continue;\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Find the actual needle run process (tmux pane_pid is the shell, not needle)\n        let needle_pid = match find_needle_process_in_tree(tmux_pid) {\n            Some(p) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    session = %session.name,\n                    tmux_pid,\n                    needle_pid = p,\n                    \"found needle run process in process tree\"\n                );\n                p\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    session = %session.name,\n                    tmux_pid,\n                    \"no needle run process found in tree, using tmux PID\"\n                );\n                tmux_pid\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Kill the entire process tree rooted at the needle run process\n        let killed = match kill_process_tree(needle_pid) {\n            Ok(k) => k,\n            Err(e) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Warning: failed to kill process tree for session '{}': {}\",\n                    session.name, e\n                );\n                false\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Verify ALL needle processes are actually gone (not just the root PID).\n        // This catches the case where new processes were spawned during the kill\n        // window or where the kill attempt didn't fully terminate the tree.\n        let remaining_processes = verify_no_needle_processes_remaining();\n        let any_remaining = !remaining_processes.is_empty();\n\n        if any_remaining {\n            println!(\n                \"Error: {} needle process(es) still running after kill attempt for session '{}':\",\n                remaining_processes.len(),\n                session.name\n            );\n            for (pid, cmdline) in &remaining_processes {\n                println!(\"  PID {}: {}\", pid, cmdline);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Kill the tmux session for cleanup\n        let kill_status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n            .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", &session.name])\n            .status();\n\n        // Clean up registry entry only if NO needle processes remain\n        if killed && !any_remaining {\n            // Extract worker identifier from session name (format: needle-<agent>-<worker_id>)\n            // Session names are sanitized: dots become underscores, so we need to handle that\n            let parts: Vec<&str> = session.name.split('-').collect();\n            let worker_id = if parts.len() >= 3 {\n                // needle-<agent>-<worker_id> -> worker_id is the third part\n                parts[2]\n            } else {\n                // Fallback: use the full session name as worker_id\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    session = %session.name,\n                    \"could not extract worker_id from session name, using full name\"\n                );\n                &session.name\n            };\n\n            let config = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n            let registry = Registry::default_location(&config.workspace.home);\n            if let Err(e) = registry.deregister(worker_id) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    worker_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to deregister worker from registry\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        match (killed, any_remaining, kill_status) {\n            (true, false, Ok(s)) if s.success() => {\n                println!(\"Stopped: {} (pid {})\", session.name, needle_pid);\n            }\n            (true, false, Ok(_)) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Stopped: {} (pid {}, session already gone)\",\n                    session.name, needle_pid\n                );\n            }\n            (true, false, Err(e)) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Warning: processes killed but failed to kill session: {}\",\n                    e\n                );\n            }\n            (false, true, _) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Error: failed to stop {} (processes still running)\",\n                    session.name\n                );\n            }\n            (true, true, _) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Error: {} - kill attempt reported success but {} process(es) still running\",\n                    session.name,\n                    remaining_processes.len()\n                );\n            }\n            (false, false, _) => {\n                println!(\"Stopped: {} (pid {} gone)\", session.name, needle_pid);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Filter sessions for cleanup based on liveness and flags.\n///\n/// This is the core filtering logic for the cleanup command, extracted to be\n/// testable. Returns the session names that should be cleaned up.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `sessions` - All discovered tmux sessions\n/// * `live_pids` - Set of PIDs that have live needle processes\n/// * `all` - If true, include all sessions regardless of liveness\n/// * `identifier` - If set, filter by identifier substring (bypasses liveness check)\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// Vector of session names to clean up\nfn filter_sessions_for_cleanup(\n    sessions: &[TmuxSession],\n    live_pids: &std::collections::HashSet<u32>,\n    all: bool,\n    identifier: &Option<String>,\n) -> Vec<String> {\n    if all {\n        // --all: remove all sessions regardless of liveness\n        sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.clone()).collect()\n    } else if let Some(id) = identifier {\n        // -i flag: filter by identifier substring (no liveness check)\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.name.contains(id))\n            .map(|s| s.name.clone())\n            .collect()\n    } else {\n        // Default: only orphaned sessions (no live backing process)\n        //\n        // IMPORTANT: tmux pane_pid returns the shell PID, not the needle binary.\n        // We must walk the process tree to find the actual needle run process\n        // before checking liveness. This matches what cmd_stop already does.\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| {\n                // Session is orphaned if:\n                // - It has no PID at all, OR\n                // - Walking from its PID finds no live needle run process\n                s.pid.map_or(true, |pane_pid| {\n                    // Try to find the actual needle run process in the tree\n                    match find_needle_process_in_tree(pane_pid) {\n                        Some(needle_pid) => !live_pids.contains(&needle_pid),\n                        None => {\n                            // No needle run found in tree — treat as orphaned\n                            // (pane_pid itself might be a dead shell wrapper)\n                            true\n                        }\n                    }\n                })\n            })\n            .map(|s| s.name.clone())\n            .collect()\n    }\n}\n\n/// `needle cleanup` — remove orphaned tmux sessions.\n///\n/// Finds and removes needle tmux sessions that no longer have active workers.\n/// With --all, removes all needle sessions regardless of worker status.\n/// With -i, filters sessions by name/identifier substring (bypasses liveness check).\nfn cmd_cleanup(all: bool, identifier: Option<String>) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No needle sessions running.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // Scan for live processes\n    let discovered = scan_needle_processes().unwrap_or_default();\n    let live_pids: std::collections::HashSet<u32> = discovered.iter().map(|p| p.pid).collect();\n\n    let targets = filter_sessions_for_cleanup(&sessions, &live_pids, all, &identifier);\n\n    if targets.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No matching sessions found.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let mut cleaned = 0;\n    for session in &targets {\n        // Kill the session\n        let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n            .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", session])\n            .status();\n\n        match status {\n            Ok(s) if s.success() => {\n                println!(\"Cleaned up: {session}\");\n                cleaned += 1;\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {\n                println!(\"Warning: session '{session}' already gone\");\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                println!(\"Warning: failed to cleanup session '{session}': {e}\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if cleaned == 0 {\n        println!(\"No sessions cleaned up.\");\n    } else {\n        println!(\"Cleaned up {cleaned} session(s).\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle list` — show running needle sessions.\nfn cmd_list(format: ListFormat) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    // ALWAYS scan process table for ALL needle run processes (both tmux and non-tmux).\n    // This ensures we discover workers regardless of how they were started.\n    let discovered = scan_needle_processes().unwrap_or_default();\n    let tmux_pids: HashSet<u32> = sessions.iter().filter_map(|s| s.pid).collect();\n\n    // Reconciliation check: compare process table against registry\n    let config = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n    let registry = Registry::default_location(&config.workspace.home);\n    let _ = reconcile_process_registry(&discovered, &registry);\n\n    // Separate discovered processes into tmux and non-tmux groups\n    let _tmux_procs: Vec<&DiscoveredProcess> = discovered\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|p| tmux_pids.contains(&p.pid))\n        .collect();\n    let orphaned: Vec<&DiscoveredProcess> = discovered\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|p| !tmux_pids.contains(&p.pid))\n        .collect();\n\n    if !orphaned.is_empty() {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            count = orphaned.len(),\n            pids = ?orphaned.iter().map(|p| p.pid).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n            \"found needle run processes not in tmux\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Show all discovered processes, not just tmux sessions\n    if sessions.is_empty() && discovered.is_empty() {\n        match format {\n            ListFormat::Table => println!(\"No needle sessions running.\"),\n            ListFormat::Json => println!(\"[]\"),\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    match format {\n        ListFormat::Table => {\n            if !sessions.is_empty() {\n                println!(\"{:<40} {:<20} {:<10}\", \"SESSION\", \"CREATED\", \"STATUS\");\n                println!(\"{}\", \"-\".repeat(70));\n                for s in &sessions {\n                    println!(\"{:<40} {:<20} {:<10}\", s.name, s.created, s.status);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // ALWAYS show discovered processes, even if they're in tmux\n            // This ensures visibility even if registry registration failed\n            if !discovered.is_empty() {\n                println!();\n                println!(\"Discovered Workers ({}):\", discovered.len());\n                println!(\"  All running needle run processes found via process table scan\");\n                for proc in &discovered {\n                    let workspace = proc\n                        .workspace\n                        .as_ref()\n                        .map(|p| p.display().to_string())\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"<unknown>\".to_string());\n                    let agent = proc.agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"<unknown>\");\n                    let identifier = proc.identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"<unknown>\");\n                    let in_tmux = if tmux_pids.contains(&proc.pid) {\n                        \" (tmux)\"\n                    } else {\n                        \" (non-tmux)\"\n                    };\n                    println!(\n                        \"  PID {} — workspace: {}, agent: {}, identifier: {}{}\",\n                        proc.pid, workspace, agent, identifier, in_tmux\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Additional warning if there are orphaned processes\n            if !orphaned.is_empty() {\n                println!();\n                println!(\"  ⚠️  {} worker(s) running outside tmux (started with NEEDLE_INNER=1 or direct invocation)\", orphaned.len());\n            }\n        }\n        ListFormat::Json => {\n            let json = serde_json::json!({\n                \"tmux_sessions\": sessions,\n                \"discovered\": discovered.iter().map(|p| {\n                    serde_json::json!({\n                        \"pid\": p.pid,\n                        \"workspace\": p.workspace,\n                        \"agent\": p.agent,\n                        \"identifier\": p.identifier,\n                        \"cmdline\": p.cmdline,\n                        \"in_tmux\": tmux_pids.contains(&p.pid),\n                    })\n                }).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n            });\n            println!(\"{}\", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&json)?);\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle init` — initialize v2 config with optional v1 migration.\n///\n/// Creates ~/.config/needle/config.yaml. let mut workspace_path = None::<PathBuf>;\n\n    // Check for v1 directory.\n    if v1_dir.exists() && v1_dir.is_dir() {\n        println!(\"Detected v1 artifacts: {}\", v1_dir.display());\n\n        // Look for v1 config hints (file-based heuristics).\n        // v1 stored agent name as a subdirectory: ~/.needle/<agent>/\n        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&v1_dir) {\n            for entry in entries.flatten() {\n                let path = entry.path();\n                if path.is_dir() {\n                    let name = path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str());\n                 .as_ref()\n                        .and_then(|p| std::fs::metadata(p).ok()?.modified().ok())\n                        .unwrap_or(std::time::SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH);\n        }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Build the config with migrated values or defaults.\n    let default_config = Config::default();\n    let agent_default = Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        bail!(\"no needle sessions running\");\n    }\n\n    // Find matching session: exact match on identifier portion or substring match on full name.\n    let matches: Vec<&TmuxSession> = sessions\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|s| s.name.ends_with(&format!(\"-{identifier}\")) || s.name.contains(identifier))\n        .collect();\n\n    if matches.is_empty() {\n        let available: Vec<&str> = sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();\n        bail!(\n            \"no session matching '{}'; available: {}\",\n            identifier,\n            available.join(\", \")\n        );\n    }\n\n    if matches.len() > 1 {\n        let names: Vec<&str> = matches.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();\n        bail!(\n            \"ambiguous identifier '{}'; matches: {}\",\n            identifier,\n            names.join(\", \")\n        );\n stats` — show outcome statistics from telemetry logs.\nfn cmd_stats(\n    by: StatsBy,\n    since: Option<String>,\n    until: Option<String>,\n    format: ListFormat,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use crate::stats::{compute_stats, StatsDimension};\n\n    let config = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n    let log_dir = config.workspace.home.join(\"logs\");\n\n    let since_dt = since.as_deref().map(telemetry::parse_since).transpose()?;\n    let until_dt = until.as_deref().map(telemetry::parse_until).transpose()?;\n    let events = telemetry::read_logs(&log_dir, since_dt,
